Uenno...she... Okay, Zojja, let's back up.  

Uenno and I decided to stay in the citadel for a few nights after we cleaned shop in the southern Shiverpeaks. Rytlock is with the others in Amnoon, apparently, so no chance of crossing paths. Uenno told me that she needed to meet with another "friend," which was starting to feel a bit suspect every other village... So I followed her. Maaaybe an invasion of privacy, but... I don't know how to feel about what happened yet.  

They met just outside of Smokestead. He looked human from a distance, but I suddenly felt  a pinch behind my left ear and sick to my stomach. Whatever spell he was using to conceal his identity was strong. The briefest flash of light, and then...a mursaat. A living mursaat. I...I'd heard about what happened with Lazarus from a Pact engineer in Lion's Arch, but...here...? I was ready to attack when he noticed my position. I tried to run, but my legs went numb.  
 
Uenno urged me to remain calm and went straight into a lecture on personal security (I don't know if it was for me or her). The mursaat hovered nearby and watched. Was he anxious...? He gently put a hand on Uenno's shoulder and pushed her aside. He knelt by me and mumbled something I couldn't make out—it didn't sound like any native tongue I'm familiar with. I could feel my legs again, though. My weapon was just out of reach, but his voice was...kind. He gave me his name and assured my safety. He already knew who I was, and he seemed honored to meet me.

strings.en:
Manikaz,  
  
Lazarus tells me you are now solely in charge of the Sanguine Crater site. I will not waste my time with congratulations; you and I both know you wished to be here, at the Door of Komalie. Our forces in the Shiverpeaks have been routed by the Shining Blade, the Deldrimor, and their allies. Some of our own have even noted that they resist our spectral magic. Secrets that were supposed to have died with the Seers.  
  
We are struggling to keep the soul batteries replenished. I suspect the forces beyond the door are working their end with increased intensity, which is why I am writing to you. Our sacrifices at Bloodstone Fen and here have not been enough. One of my little mice in the grass tells me you are researching a potential connection between bloodstones. An easier way to transport souls betwixt shards. Should this be true, then consider this next statement an official directive.  
  
You are to commence with further sacrifices, starting with the remaining humans and kodan. Once they are gone, begin to round up our dissidents, the insane, and the weak. They will have the privilege of serving the cause. If you do this, Lazarus and I will see that your discovery is lauded for centuries.  
  
Be prepared to transfer the souls to the Komalie site. Do not fail us.  
  
Mercia

After being called to collaborate on the fractal incursion cleanup, I spent some time researching our enigmatic ally, the Mist Stranger. They have appeared to aid the wayfinder in several instances, most notably the Mists disturbance involving Scarlet Briar's twisted marionette construct (see attached records). However, it appears that a request from Isgarren himself has placed more detailed information at the highest level of secrecy.

I will briefly enumerate the key points available. The Mist Stranger appears to be a unique entity born of the Mists, humanoid in appearance but alien in biology. They exhibit an extremely strong familiarity with their native environment, but their actions suggest that they are primarily concerned with Tyria and that their goals are aligned with the Astral Ward's. They consistently cultivate allies among Tyria's citizens and offer assistance rather than direct intervention.

After careful consideration, the Astral Ward does not categorize this Mist being as an intruder to Tyria. Theirs is a highly atypical case, and I can only speculate that the wizards have context I am not privy to that marks the stranger as an unquestionable ally.

—Field Archivist Cierle
